# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 77 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 77 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_077_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 7

**1** After a few days I saw him in the same plain where I had also seen the shepherds; and he said to me, "What do you seek?" **2** I said to him, "Lord, I ask that you command the shepherd who punishes to depart from my house, for he greatly afflicts me." **3** "It is necessary for you to be afflicted," he replied, "for thus the glorious angel commanded regarding you, wishing that you should be tested." **4** "But why, Lord? What evil have I done that I am handed over to this angel?" **5** "Listen," he said; "your sins are indeed many, yet not so many that you must be delivered to this angel; but your household has committed great iniquities and sins, and the glorious angel has been embittered over their deeds, and so he commanded that you be afflicted for a time, so that they too might repent and be purified from every worldly desire. **6** When they repent and are purified, the angel of punishment will depart." **7** I asked him, "Lord, if they have acted in such a way that the glorious angel has been embittered, what have I done?" He replied, "There is no other way they can be afflicted unless you, as head of the household, are afflicted; for when you are afflicted, they are necessarily afflicted as well — but when you prosper, they cannot experience affliction." **8** I said, "But Lord, behold, they have repented with their whole heart." **9** "I know," he said, "that they have repented with their whole heart. But do you suppose the sins of those who repent are immediately forgiven? Not at all — the one who repents must discipline his own soul and be profoundly humbled in all his actions and suffer many forms of affliction. And if he endures the afflictions that come upon him, he who created all things and invested them with power will surely be moved to compassion and grant some remedy. **10** And this will happen when he sees the heart of every penitent clean from every evil. It is therefore beneficial for you and your household to be afflicted now. But why do I say so much? You must be afflicted as the angel of the Lord has commanded — he who delivered you to me. And give thanks to the Lord for this, that he judged you worthy to reveal the affliction to you beforehand, so that knowing it in advance you might endure it with strength."

---

*LOGOS maintains formal equivalence. "Embittered" renders the Greek verb pikrainō. "Head of household" renders the implied oikos leadership role.*
